reforms.description: The Administration has proposed increases in Federal support of R&D, most recently in the 2015 Budget proposal of USD 135.4 billion, alongside the creation of an Energy Security Trust Fund to support innovation in energy-saving technology and low carbon technology. Additionally, the America COMPETES Act established the Advanced Research Projects Agency–Energy, which funds energy technology projects to promote innovation in energy efficiency and low carbon technology.
reforms.package_name: Federal R&D and Energy Innovation Support
reforms.component_name: R&D Funding and Energy Trust Fund
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Increased funding for R&D and energy innovation is expected to enhance productivity and technological advancement.
reforms.status_evidence: The proposals are part of the 2015 Budget and other announcements.
reforms.importance_rationale: The reforms represent significant increases in federal R&D funding and the establishment of a dedicated trust fund for energy innovation.
reforms.source_quote: The Administration has proposed increases in Federal support of R&D, most recently in the 2015 Budget proposal of USD 135.4 billion, a nominal increase of 1.2% over 2014.

reforms.description: The US is taking policy actions to improve quality secondary education, based on the recommendations of the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology (PCAST) 2010 report Prepare and Inspire, including supporting state-led standards for secondary education and making investments toward preparing 100,000 more STEM-qualified teachers over the next decade.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Investing in STEM education is expected to enhance the quality of the workforce and support innovation.
reforms.status_evidence: The actions are based on recommendations and are part of ongoing policy efforts.
reforms.importance_rationale: The initiative aims to significantly improve the quality of secondary education and increase the number of qualified STEM teachers.
reforms.source_quote: The US is taking policy actions to improve quality secondary education, based on the recommendations of the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology (PCAST) 2010 report Prepare and Inspire.

reforms.description: Under the Administration’s Preschool for All initiative, States would need to meet quality standards to receive federal funds, including requiring preschool teachers to have a bachelor degree and ongoing professional development, as well as requiring higher preschool staff salaries.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Improving preschool education quality is expected to enhance early childhood education outcomes and support future innovation.
reforms.status_evidence: The initiative is part of the Administration's proposals for early childhood education.
reforms.importance_rationale: The initiative represents a significant policy change aimed at improving early childhood education standards.
reforms.source_quote: Under the Administration’s Preschool for All initiative, States would need to meet quality standards to receive federal funds, including requiring preschool teachers to have a bachelor degree and ongoing professional development.
